source_text: Patefacta igitur vel imperitia vel impudentia tua, quae aut non curat aut non valet, quid dicatur, exponere, ostensoque veritatis ipsius, quam se esse Christus appellavit [n208] , lumine nihil de apostoli Pauli sermonibus Manichaeae id est vestrae cohaerere dementiae, nunc expositioni operam demus, ut, sicut ostensum est, qualiter non possit, ita clareat, qualiter et debeat Paulus et possit intellegi.
pass_a_gloss: Your unskillfulness or shamelessness therefore having been opened, which either does not care or is not able to explain what is said, and the light of truth itself, which Christ called himself, having been shown to cohere with nothing of the apostle Paul's speeches of Manichaean, that is your, madness, let us now give work to exposition, so that, as it has been shown how he cannot, so it may become clear how Paul both ought and can be understood.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: Your ignorance or shamelessness is therefore exposed: either you do not care to explain what is said, or you cannot. The light of truth itself—which Christ called himself (John 14:6)—has shown that nothing in the apostle Paul’s words agrees with the Manichaeans’ madness, that is, yours. Let us now devote ourselves to explanation. Just as we have shown how Paul cannot be understood, let it also become clear how he should and can be understood.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
